findings.title: The profile gate accepts the seeded company name and the seeded terms, so a new franchise sends quotes naming 'Koala Insulation of Newark'
findings.failureScenario: Every database gets branding.company = 'Koala Insulation of Newark' (init.sql:1138, description 'PLACEHOLDER — PDF branding'). It also gets quote_terms 'A signed quote authorizes Koala Insulation of Newark to schedule the work…' (phase1.sql:16, description 'PLACEHOLDER, owner to replace'). isGap (profile.ts:56-61) only looks for an empty value or the word 'placeholder' inside the value. Take a Springfield, IL franchise. It is told to 'add the license number, the office phone, the state and the warranty', fills exactly those, and sees the green 'Everything a quote needs is filled in.' Its quotes then go out under the Newark company name, with terms that authorize Koala Insulation of Newark to do the work. Ledger L30 says a required field that is 'still a seed PLACEHOLDER' blocks sending, but two of the seven required fields are not checked that way. Expected: the seeded company and terms count as gaps until the owner saves them.
findings.evidence: Scratch vitest /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/accuracy/revA/documents/zz-review-tests/documents.test.ts, test 'the gate names only license, phone, state and warranty; the seeded company and terms pass' (passes, which confirms the behaviour). On the seed rows, businessProfileGaps gives exactly those 4 gaps. After license, phone, IL and warranty are filled it gives []. quoteSettingsFromRows(filled).branding.company is 'Koala Insulation of Newark', terms contain 'authorizes Koala Insulation of Newark', and newEstimateDefaults gives {city:'Newark', state:'IL'}. Run with: npx vitest run lib/zz-review (in a worktree at fdc3eaa).
findings.suggestedFix: Treat a profile setting as a gap while its app_settings.description still marks it as a seed PLACEHOLDER. saveSettings already strips that marker when the owner saves (stripPlaceholder), so one save of the Business profile clears it. Alternatively, require an explicit owner confirmation of company and terms. Production would then also need the owner to re-save the terms once.

findings.title: New estimates take the town from the shop address and the state from the profile, giving a wrong pair (Newark, PA / Newark, IL)
findings.failureScenario: newEstimateDefaults (profile.ts:93-101) falls back field by field. Take a profile with State = PA and Town left empty (the page says 'Left empty, they take the town of the shop address'), and the seeded shop_address 'Newark, DE 19711' (description still 'PLACEHOLDER, set the shop address'). Every new estimate then starts in 'Newark, PA'. A franchise licensed in one state with its shop in another hits the same thing: shop 'Philadelphia, PA' with state NJ gives 'Philadelphia, NJ'. If the estimator does not retype the town, the quote's property line prints the wrong town and state. Ledger L32 says 'the profile's town and state, else the shop address's'; the code mixes the two.
findings.evidence: Same scratch vitest file, test 'town from the shop address and state from the profile are mixed when they differ': production rows plus default_state PA give {city:'Newark', state:'PA'}. The seed-franchise test gives {city:'Newark', state:'IL'}.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose the place as a pair: use the profile town with the profile state; else use the shop address's town only when its state equals the profile state (or there is no profile state); else leave the town blank and use the profile state. Ignore a shop_address whose description still says PLACEHOLDER.

findings.title: L39 keep-together: an option of 18 lines or fewer that is taller than a page prints with overlapping, unreadable lines
findings.failureScenario: OptionSection sets wrap={false} whenever items plus bullets is 18 or fewer, whatever the text length. When such a block is taller than a page, react-pdf logs 'Node of type VIEW can't wrap between pages and it's bigger than available page height' and squeezes the block: bullets and area names print on top of each other on the customer's PDF. Two inputs that trigger it, both within the app's limits: (a) 12 items with 80-character area names (the draft schema allows 80) plus 6 owner bullets of 200 characters (the admin form allows 8 x 200); (b) 17 items with 75-character descriptions and 50-character area names plus 1 bullet. Real engine quotes with 8 areas and long names did not trigger it, so this is an edge case. Before this stage such a block would have broken across pages normally.
findings.evidence: Scratch script /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/accuracy/revA/documents/zz-review-scripts/pdf-tall.ts, run with node scripts/accuracy/run.mjs on a worktree at fdc3eaa. Args '12 6 70 200 80' and '17 1 75 100 50' print the react-pdf warning. Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/accuracy/revA/documents/tall-12-6-1.png shows the Better block with overlapping bullets and area names; the PDF is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/e9b02a42-cb4a-5aa1-bf7b-e82e27ad6b23/scratchpad/accuracy/revA/documents/tall-12-6.pdf.
